question: Grok recommends excluding memecoins and penny stocks from all production universes; the registry carries nine live entries in exactly those classes.
meaning: The nine hypotheses stay in the registry (M-107 requires the trial record to survive) but are NOT production-eligible: they may not be promoted, sized, or added to a live scanner universe until a separate pre-registered decision reverses this.
rationale: measured: MEME n=10, PF 0.023 in the class-divergence audit - the worst cell in the book
measured: PENNY n=4 with spreads that exceed the median target move at any size we can trade
structural: no survivorship-free delisted dataset, so every backtest on these universes is flattered
Grok, Subq and our own edge backlog independently reach the same conclusion
reversal_condition: a survivorship-free point-in-time universe exists AND a pre-registered hypothesis clears the full promotion gate (forward n>=200, net CI>0 at 2x cost, DSR>=0.95)

addenda.what: H-215 (penny tsmom_12_1 long/flat) and H-219 (penny xsmom top2 6m) from the per-class sweep H-200..H-221 were live registry entries with no ruling, which is what made test_policy_covers_every_live_entry fail. Both are ruled RESEARCH_ONLY by the decision above, not by a new decision: the ruling is a property of the CLASS, and the reason it now bites is that these two cells were INSUFFICIENT_N (labelled, not dropped). No new evidence exists for either, and neither may be promoted under this ruling.
